• The High Court can review the decisions of the Governor or Election Commission if they are challenged.

• **State Election Commission**
 
 
• The **State Election Commission** is responsible for conducting local body elections and does not decide the disqualification of State Legislative Assembly members.
 
• Its primary role is to oversee elections for municipalities, panchayats, and other local governance bodies.
 
• Disqualification of state legislators falls under the purview of the **Election Commission of India** and the Governor.

__
 
• 
 
**Financial Emergency:**

 
 
• A Financial Emergency is imposed under Article 360 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is declared when the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• During a Financial Emergency, the central government can give directions to states to observe specified canons of financial propriety.
 
• Salaries and allowances of any class of persons serving in connection with the affairs of the Union and the Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts can be reduced.
 
• It is designed to protect the economic stability of the nation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**President’s Rule:**

 
 
• President’s Rule is imposed under Article 356 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is declared when the President is satisfied that the government of a state cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• It leads to the suspension of the state government and the imposition of direct rule by the central government.
 
• It is related to the breakdown of the constitutional machinery in a state.
 
• It is not related to financial stability.
 
 
 
• 
 
**National Emergency:**

 
 
• A National Emergency is imposed under Article 352 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is declared when there is a threat to the security of India or any part of its territory due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• It affects the fundamental rights of citizens and the distribution of powers between the center and the states.
 
• It is related to national security, not financial stability.
 
• This emergency has been declared several times in India's history.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Internal Emergency:**

 
 
• The term "Internal Emergency" is usually associated with the National Emergency declared in 1975, which was imposed on the grounds of "internal disturbance."
 
• This type of emergency is now covered under Article 352, which, after amendments, requires the threat to be due to "armed rebellion" rather than "internal disturbance."
 
• It is related to internal security, not directly to economic stability.

• The emergency declared in 1975, is a very controversial part of Indian history.

questions.question: Which of the following is a salient feature of the Indian Constitution?

• The constitution establishes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.

• The constitution also outlines the federal structure of India, dividing powers between the central and state governments.
 
• The judiciary plays a crucial role in interpreting and upholding the constitution.
 
• The constitution is the supreme law of the land, and all other laws must conform to it.
 
• The constitution reflects the aspirations and values of the Indian people.
 
• It aims to create a just and equitable society.
 
• It is a living document that continues to shape the destiny of India.

questions.question: ‘Beri-Beri’ is caused by the deficiency of __________.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Thiamine:**

 
 
• Thiamine, also known as Vitamin B1, is essential for energy metabolism and nerve function.
 
• A deficiency of thiamine leads to Beri-Beri.
 
• Beri-Beri can manifest in various forms, including wet Beri-Beri (affecting the cardiovascular system) and dry Beri-Beri (affecting the nervous system).
 
• Symptoms include muscle weakness, fatigue, and neurological problems.
 
• Thiamine is found in foods like whole grains, legumes, and pork.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Riboflavin:**

 
 
• Riboflavin, or Vitamin B2, is important for cell growth and energy production.
 
• A deficiency of riboflavin can cause conditions like cheilosis (cracked lips) and glossitis (inflamed tongue).
 
• It is vital for healthy skin and eyes.
 
• It is found in dairy products, eggs, and leafy green vegetables.
 
• It also helps with the metabolism of fats.
 
 
 
• **Cyanocobalamin:**
 
 
• Cyanocobalamin, or Vitamin B12, is crucial for red blood cell formation and nerve function.
 
• A deficiency of Vitamin B12 can lead to anemia and neurological problems.
 
• It is primarily found in animal products like meat, fish, and dairy.
 
• It is essential for DNA synthesis.
 
• Vegetarians and vegans may need to supplement their diet with B12.
 
 
 
• **Niacin:**
 
 
• Niacin, or Vitamin B3, is involved in energy metabolism and DNA repair.
 
• A deficiency of niacin causes Pellagra, which is characterized by dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia.
 
• It is important for healthy skin and the nervous system.
 
• Niacin is found in foods like meat, poultry, and grains.
 
• It can also be produced by the body from the amino acid tryptophan

questions.question: The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force in the direction of force. This is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**second law of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• 
 
**second law of motion:**

 
 
• Newton's second law of motion states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced force and takes place in the direction of the force.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as F = ma, where F is the force, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.
 
• This law explains how forces cause changes in motion.
 
• It is the fundamental law that relates force to acceleration.
 
• The change of momentum is equal to the impulse of the force.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**law of inertia:**

 
 
• The law of inertia is also known as Newton's first law of motion.
 
• It states that an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion with a constant velocity, unless acted upon by an unbalanced force. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• It describes the tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion.
 
• It is the law that defines inertia.
 
• Inertia is the resistance of any physical object to any change in its velocity.
 
 
 
• 
 
**first law of motion:**

 
 
• Newton's first law of motion is essentially the law of inertia.
 
• It defines inertia and explains how objects behave in the absence of external forces.
 
• It sets the foundation for understanding how forces affect motion.
 
• It is the law of unforced motion.
 
• An object will continue to do whatever it is doing, until a force acts upon it.
 
 
 
• 
 
**third law of motion:**

 
 
• Newton's third law of motion states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• This means that when one object exerts a force on another object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first object. 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
• This law explains how forces occur in pairs.
 
• It is the law of action and reaction.
 
• Forces always come in pairs.
